confidence_notes: I used six web searches: one for the RBA rate and five for prices. The RBA rate comes from a search result summarising the RBA exchange-rates table, not from a page I opened. Coffee, beer and restaurant meals rest on city-level aggregator pages for Jeonju (CityCost, Expatistan, a Jeonju nightlife guide, Cities Insider), which are crowdsourced or modelled and not always dated. They broadly agree: cappuccino about KRW 4,700-5,000, pub domestic beer KRW 4,500-6,000, budget meal about KRW 9,400-10,000, and mid-range dinner for two about KRW 30,000-41,000. I raised the mid-range figure a little because the aggregator averages look low for a sit-down three-course meal. I found no Jeonju-specific cocktail or wine-by-the-glass price. The cocktail is anchored on the Seoul Expatistan average (about KRW 12,000), discounted for a smaller city. The wine glass is set at roughly 1.8-2x the beer price, as Korean restaurants typically price it. I assumed about KRW 1,450-1,500 per USD. Accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge of Jeonju, which has a hanok-village guesthouse market and modest business hotels. I did not search for accommodation prices or inspect any listings, so those four are the least certain.
comparable_city_reasoning: Jeonju is a mid-sized South Korean provincial city and a domestic tourism and food destination. Its prices sit below Seoul, roughly 15-30% lower for restaurants and bars and more for lodging, and are comparable to Gwangju, Daegu and other regional Korean cities.
